---
title: "xenium_nb — QC"
subtitle: "Per-cell QC distributions and QC in tissue, one section per sample"
# Pin the kernel by name, as cluster_report.qmd does. Apptainer bind-mounts $HOME, so
# kernelspecs from ~/.local/share/jupyter/kernels shadow the container's own — quarto's
# default "python3" then resolves to a host env missing the pipeline's packages, and
# every cell fails at import under `error: true` while the render still exits 0.
jupyter: python_spatial
format:
  pptx:
    reference-doc: ouhsc_ppt_template.pptx
    # `#` becomes a Section Header slide, `##` a Title-and-Content slide. Without
    # this pandoc infers the level from the headings present, so adding the first
    # `#` would silently demote every `##` to a bullet.
    slide-level: 2
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  # Keep rendering when a cell raises: one sample's panel erroring leaves an error slide
  # in its own section instead of taking the whole deck down. The cost is that a
  # genuinely broken cell yields an error slide and an exit code of 0 — read the slides,
  # not just the exit status.
  error: true
---

```{python}
# | tags: [setup]
import traceback
from pathlib import Path

import anndata as ad
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import numpy as np
import zarr
from IPython.display import display, Markdown
from matplotlib.colors import LogNorm

# The reference template is 16:9 at 10 x 5.625in; leave room for a slide title.
FIGSIZE = (9.0, 4.3)
# Inches reserved beside the in-tissue plots for their colorbar, which sits outside
# the axes and would otherwise be cropped by tight_layout.
LEGEND_WIDTH = 1.4
# Fraction of the in-tissue axes the cell dots should cover, which sets their size.
SPATIAL_COVERAGE = 0.45

# Every raw zarr is staged into this notebook's working directory by the Nextflow
# process, so globbing is the whole input contract — no params to pass or drift.
#
# These are create_sdata's zarrs, NOT cluster_sdata's: nothing here has been filtered
# yet, which is the point. Reading this deck off clustered zarrs would show only the
# cells that survived the min_counts cut, with the discarded tail already gone — so the
# distributions would look clean no matter how much was thrown away.
ZARRS = sorted(Path(".").glob("*.zarr"))
if not ZARRS:
    raise FileNotFoundError("No .zarr directories staged next to the notebook.")

# The per-cell QC columns each sample's distribution panel shows, as
# (obs column, axis label, log scale).
#
# All four come straight from the zarr — create_sdata annotates the transcript and gene
# counts, and the Xenium reader supplies both areas from cells.parquet. This deck derives
# nothing.
QC_COLUMNS = [
    ("transcript_counts", "Transcripts per cell", True),
    ("n_genes_by_transcripts", "Genes per cell", True),
    ("cell_area", "Cell area (µm²)", True),
    ("nucleus_area", "Nucleus area (µm²)", True),
]

# Every obs column this deck reads, checked against each zarr in the loop below. All of
# them come from create_sdata or the Xenium reader; none is derived here. Listing them in
# one place means a zarr that predates a column fails on the first sample with the column
# named, rather than several slides later inside whichever panel happened to want it.
REQUIRED_OBS = [col for col, _, _ in QC_COLUMNS] + ["sample"]


def log_hist(ax, values, label, log):
    """One QC distribution panel, with its median marked.

    Non-positive values are dropped from a log panel rather than silently shifting the
    whole distribution to make them plottable: transcript_counts reaches 0 on real data,
    and nucleus_area is 0 for every cell segmented without a nucleus. Both are exactly
    the cells a QC deck must not hide, so the count that fell off is printed in the panel
    title instead of being folded into the first bin.
    """
    values = np.asarray(values, dtype=float)
    values = values[np.isfinite(values)]
    if log:
        positive = values[values > 0]
        n_dropped = len(values) - len(positive)
        bins = np.logspace(np.log10(positive.min()), np.log10(positive.max()), 60)
        ax.set_xscale("log")
    else:
        positive, n_dropped, bins = values, 0, 60

    ax.hist(positive, bins=bins, color="#4C72B0")
    median = float(np.median(values))
    ax.axvline(median, color="#C44E52", lw=1.2)
    ax.set_xlabel(label, size=7)
    ax.set_ylabel("Cells", size=7)
    title = f"median {median:,.0f}"
    if n_dropped:
        title += f" · {n_dropped:,} at zero"
    ax.set_title(title, size=7)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
    ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)


def point_size(ax, n_cells, coverage=SPATIAL_COVERAGE):
    """Marker area (pt²) that lets n_cells cover `coverage` of these axes, once.

    A fixed size cannot serve every tissue plot: at s=3 a 21k-cell strip reads well but a
    32k-cell section is a solid mat of dots, and at s=1 the strip is speckle. Taking the
    axes' own area covers both — get_position() is the pre-tight_layout fraction of the
    figure, close enough for a marker size. 72 pt to the inch, squared, converts inches²
    to the pt² units scatter's `s` is in.
    """
    w, h = ax.get_figure().get_size_inches()
    pos = ax.get_position()
    area_pt2 = (pos.width * w) * (pos.height * h) * 72 ** 2
    return float(np.clip(coverage * area_pt2 / n_cells, 0.5, 6.0))


def tissue_figure(obs, n):
    """A figure holding `n` tissue panels, laid out and sized to fill the slide.

    A fixed FIGSIZE wastes the slide on anything that is not 2:1: a tall section renders
    as a sliver down the middle of a wide figure, because set_aspect("equal") is
    non-negotiable for tissue. Sizing the figure to the data's aspect instead means the
    image pandoc embeds is all tissue, and PowerPoint centres it on the slide.

    The ORIENTATION has to follow the tissue too, which is why this does not just take a
    column count. These ROIs are wide strips (~3:1), and two of those side by side make a
    6:1 figure that pandoc scales to the slide width — leaving two panels about a
    centimetre tall in a band of whitespace. Stacking the same two panels gives 1.5:1,
    close to the slide's own proportions, and each panel keeps real estate. A tall tissue
    inverts the argument, so the layout is chosen per sample rather than fixed: whichever
    of the two arrangements lands closest to the slide's aspect wins, compared in log
    space so being twice too wide and half too wide count equally.
    """
    aspect = np.ptp(obs["spatial_x"]) / np.ptp(obs["spatial_y"])
    box_w, box_h = FIGSIZE[0] - LEGEND_WIDTH, FIGSIZE[1]
    target = box_w / box_h

    nrows, ncols = min([(1, n), (n, 1)],
                       key=lambda rc: abs(np.log(aspect * rc[1] / rc[0] / target)))
    combined = aspect * ncols / nrows
    # Fit the combined block inside the slide's plot box, touching whichever edge binds.
    w, h = (box_w, box_w / combined) if combined >= target else (box_h * combined, box_h)
    return plt.subplots(nrows, ncols, figsize=(w + LEGEND_WIDTH, h), squeeze=False)


# ── Slides ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# One function per slide, each emitting its own heading, caption, and figure. The
# per-sample loop below is then literally a list of the slides in the order they appear,
# and adding or reordering one is a line there rather than a block edit. Keeping the
# caption next to the figure it describes is the other half of it — the two are edited
# together far more often than either is edited alone.


def qc_histogram_slide(obs, sample):
    """Slide: this sample's per-cell QC, one histogram per metric.

    A 2x2 grid over QC_COLUMNS, so adding or dropping a metric there changes the slide
    without touching this function. Leftover axes are removed rather than hidden — a
    hidden axes still reserves its cell under tight_layout and squeezes the real panels
    into a fraction of the slide.

    Per-panel scaling, the median line, and the zero handling live in log_hist; what this
    owns is the grid, the caption, and the slide title.
    """
    display(Markdown("## Per-cell QC distributions"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Distributions of transcripts, genes detected, cell area, and nucleus area "
        "across all cells in this sample, before any filtering. All four are on log "
        "axes; the red line marks each median. Cells at zero cannot be drawn on a log "
        "axis and are counted in the panel title instead."
    ))

    fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 2, figsize=FIGSIZE, squeeze=False)
    for ax, (col, label, log) in zip(axes.ravel(), QC_COLUMNS):
        log_hist(ax, obs[col], label, log)
    for ax in axes.ravel()[len(QC_COLUMNS):]:
        fig.delaxes(ax)

    fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(obs):,} cells", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)


def qc_tissue_scatter_slide(obs, sample):
    """Slide: this sample's cells in tissue, coloured by transcripts and by genes.

    The two panels are the same scatter with a different colour column, so they are a
    loop rather than two blocks — they cannot drift apart in marker size, aspect, or
    colour scaling. Layout and figure size come from tissue_figure, which picks 1x2 or
    2x1 from the tissue's own aspect.

    Both columns reach zero on real data and LogNorm rejects a zero vmin, so the colour
    floor is clipped to 1: those cells stay drawn at the bottom of the ramp instead of
    dropping out of the panel that exists to locate them.
    """
    display(Markdown("## QC in tissue coordinates"))
    display(Markdown(
        "Every cell at its position on the slide, coloured by transcript count and by "
        "genes detected, both on log colour scales. Axes are in µm and share an equal "
        "aspect, so the panels are at tissue proportions."
    ))

    fig, axes = tissue_figure(obs, 2)
    panels = [
        ("transcript_counts", "Transcripts"),
        ("n_genes_by_transcripts", "Genes"),
    ]
    for ax, (col, label) in zip(axes.ravel(), panels):
        values = obs[col].to_numpy(dtype=float)
        im = ax.scatter(
            obs["spatial_x"], obs["spatial_y"],
            c=np.clip(values, 1, None),
            s=point_size(ax, len(obs)),
            cmap="viridis",
            norm=LogNorm(vmin=1, vmax=max(values.max(), 2)),
            linewidths=0,
        )
        ax.set_aspect("equal")
        # Slide y runs downward in Xenium's frame; inverting keeps the tissue the way
        # round it appears in Xenium Explorer.
        ax.invert_yaxis()
        ax.set_title(label, size=8)
        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)
        cbar = fig.colorbar(im, ax=ax, fraction=0.046, pad=0.02)
        cbar.ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)

    fig.suptitle(f"{sample} · {len(obs):,} cells", fontsize=9, x=0.01, ha="left")
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()
    plt.close(fig)
```

```{python}
# One `# <sample>` section per sample, driven by the staged zarrs rather than a hardcoded
# block each: the cohort changes, and a hardcoded list silently omits a new sample while
# raising KeyError on a removed one.
#
# Each sample's obs is dropped as soon as its two slides are drawn, so a cohort's worth
# of obs frames is never co-resident.
#
# Every heading here and in the slide functions is emitted with display(Markdown(...))
# from an ORDINARY cell, NOT under `output: asis`. Under asis everything a cell displays
# concatenates into one raw markdown stream: the figure lands between the blocks and
# leaves the next heading not starting its own line, so pandoc prints a literal "## ..."
# as text and drops the image entirely. display(Markdown) does not hit it — each call
# emits its own complete block, and each figure ends with plt.show() so it lands
# between them.
for path in ZARRS:
    # Read obs and the spatial coordinates, and nothing else. ad.io.read_elem on the
    # table's zarr groups leaves the count matrix on disk, which this deck never needs —
    # every metric it shows was annotated by create_sdata at the one point X was in
    # memory. spatialdata.read_zarr would instead materialize every image, point, and
    # shape per sample, the difference between a deck that renders on a laptop and one
    # that does not.
    store = zarr.open(f"{path}/tables/table", mode="r")
    obs = ad.io.read_elem(store["obs"])

    # Coordinates live in obsm; copying them into obs is the only change made to the
    # data anywhere in this deck, and it exists so the tissue slide can plot position
    # and QC from a single frame.
    spatial = ad.io.read_elem(store["obsm"]["spatial"])
    obs["spatial_x"] = spatial[:, 0]
    obs["spatial_y"] = spatial[:, 1]

    # This deck computes no QC metric of its own, and has no fallbacks. A report that
    # derives a metric is a second definition of it, and the two drift without anything
    # saying so; a fallback is that second definition wearing a disguise, letting a stale
    # cohort render a deck whose numbers came from outside the pipeline. Failing here
    # names the fix, which is to re-run create_sdata.
    #
    # Outside the per-sample try below, deliberately: a missing column means the whole
    # cohort came from a create_sdata that predates it, so failing the render outright is
    # more useful than a traceback slide repeated once per sample.
    missing = [c for c in REQUIRED_OBS if c not in obs.columns]
    if missing:
        raise KeyError(
            f"{Path(path).name}: obs is missing {missing}. These come from create_sdata "
            "— re-run it over this sample rather than deriving them here."
        )

    # obs["sample"] is written by create_sdata, so the sample id comes from the object
    # rather than the staged path — which is a meaningless sample1.zarr, since the
    # process stages every zarr under an indexed name.
    sample = str(obs["sample"].iloc[0])

    display(Markdown(f"# {sample}"))

    # The slides, in the order they appear, each caught independently. This loop is a
    # single cell, so anything raising without being caught aborts the cell and drops
    # every LATER sample from the deck too — with the render still exiting 0 under
    # `error: true`.
    #
    # Per slide rather than per sample because these slides share nothing: each reads obs
    # and derives its own figure, so one failing says nothing about the others. Catching
    # here also puts the traceback under the failed slide's OWN title, since every slide
    # function emits its heading before it plots — which names the broken slide instead
    # of leaving a traceback loose in the section.
    #
    # (A deck whose slides read shared derived state — a correlation matrix feeding three
    # slides, say — wants one try around that computation instead: if it fails, every
    # slide downstream of it is meaningless and should be skipped together.)
    for slide in (qc_histogram_slide, qc_tissue_scatter_slide):
        try:
            slide(obs, sample)
        except Exception:
            # close(), not close(fig): the slide raised before reaching its own close,
            # so the half-built figure is still open and unreachable from here.
            plt.close()
            display(Markdown(f"```\n{traceback.format_exc()}\n```"))

    del obs
```
